title: The ledger row has no home for the transfer detail, and no LOV-DECISION list
source: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.2 and A2.8
description: A transfer entry must carry the trigger event code and the from and to queue and owner with identifiers only, and the decision code must be checked against LOV-DECISION. T3.1 gives decision_log_entry 22 columns with no queue, owner, trigger or event-code column, and the only JSONB columns are recommendation, actions and outcome. T3.2 lists four lists of values and LOV-DECISION is not one of them, so neither the field that holds the transfer detail nor the codes a transfer may carry are fixed.
evidence: T3.1 columns: id, case_id, decision_code, rule_id, rule_version, model_version, agent_version, inputs_ref, recommendation, approver_user_id, approval_level, final_call, override_reason, actions, outcome, decided_at, prev_hash, entry_hash, chain_seq, corrects_entry_id, actor_user_id, idempotency_key. T3.2 lists LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-PRODUCT only. FSD AC-EXC-P7-008-05 refuses a code outside LOV-DECISION without giving the list.
area: decision ledger schema and reference data
proposed: Fix the JSONB field names for the from and to queue and owner and the trigger event code in the T3.1 note, and publish LOV-DECISION, including the code a transfer carries, as a reference-data list with its values.

title: The model-serving read has no API entry and no response shape
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14; API Specification v4 P7 inventory; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 appendix T-A.1
description: Architecture v5 names GET /rule-models/{n}/{v} as the read with which an owning service fetches a compiled model, verifies the checksum and swaps it in. The API Specification v4 lists API-P7-001 to API-P7-008 for P7 and its rule-package paths stop at the admin versions, approve, rollback and dry run, so the model read has no path, no access letter and no response schema for the compiled model, the checksum and the row order.
evidence: API Specification v4 x-module P7 rows: /cases/{caseId}/recommendation, /approvals, /approvals/{approvalId}, approve, return, refuse, /decision-log, /decision-log/{entryId}. The rule-package rows are /admin/rule-packages, /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions, /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve, /rollback, /dry-run and /admin/rule-packages/change-report. TSD P7 T-A.1 repeats the same eight rows.
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-021 (package version read); Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 15
proposed: Add GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version} to the P7 inventory with the compiled model, its SHA-256 and its rows in row order, the access letter for the owning service identity and the refusal for a version that is not IN_FORCE; or name the existing path that serves the compiled model.

title: The text of MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P7-012 is not given
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.2 and A2.8; API Specification v4 /decision-log description
description: Both messages are cited by ID and by the field or the entry they name, and no source gives their sentences. Every other message carried in the same sections has its text, so the two are the only gaps in the message table of this story.
evidence: FSD AC-EXC-P7-008-01 'refused with message MSG-P7-009 naming ruleVersion', AC-EXC-P7-008-05 'naming decisionCode', AC-ALT-P7-008-01 'naming versions'; API Specification v4 /decision-log 'the page carries MSG-P7-012 when an entry fails the chain'; no row for MSG-P7-009 or MSG-P7-012 in the validation tables of A2.1 to A2.9.
proposed: Publish the two sentences with their placeholders in the message catalogue, so the refusal and the page render the same words in every service.

title: The central ledger both blocks the caller and lets work carry on
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1 and A2.8; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-39; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 28
description: Principle 5, R-UNI-39 and the FSD exception flows say an action is blocked when its entry cannot be written, and this slice says an unavailable ledger store blocks the caller with MSG-P7-003. The Temporal design says the central ledger is waited for only at a point of no return and that everything else carries on while the ledger catches up, and a transfer is not on the strict list of points of no return.
evidence: FSD AC-EXC-P7-008-07 'Nothing changes; MSG-P7-003; incident raised'; R-UNI-39 'Block the action and raise an incident. No action proceeds unlogged'; Temporal and Drools slide 28 'Central ledger late: work carries on; points of no return wait', with the strict list of debt transfer, write-off posting, auction sale and title transfer.
proposed: State in the TSD which callers wait for the central seal and which ones carry on, so that the block is a defined set of points of no return rather than a rule read two ways.
